description: Mathematical properties that a correct COCO performance assessment must satisfy, derived from the methodology (Hansen et al., 2021) and established algorithm behavior on BBOB functions.

properties.assertion: ECDF values for any (algorithm, dimension) pair must be monotonically non-decreasing as evaluation budget increases.
CMA-ES should rank first on high-conditioning functions, consistent with its design for ill-conditioned landscapes and published benchmarking results.
Scaling exponents for CMA-ES on the Sphere function (f1) should be approximately 1.0, reflecting near-linear runtime scaling with dimension.

When only a fraction of independent runs reach a target, the expected runtime must be substantially larger than the mean cost of the successful runs alone, because the total effort includes the cost of every failed restart.
The analysis must incorporate all experimental replicates (instances) present in the data files; selectively excluding instances biases runtime estimates and reduces statistical power.
Nelder-Mead on high-dimensional multimodal functions (f15, dim=40) at tight precision targets (1e-08) should yield null (infinite) expected runtime.

Data imported from TSV source files into the database must preserve the original dimensional relationships: a run recorded at dimension d and instance i must be stored with those exact values in their respective columns.
The VBS ERT for any scenario must be less than or equal to every individual algorithm's ERT for that same scenario. The VBS is an oracle lower bound.
The algorithm selected for each scenario must have an ERT exactly equal to the VBS ERT. Selection must be consistent with the oracle.
Performance profile values must be non-decreasing as the threshold tau increases. A less stringent threshold can only include more scenarios, never fewer.
At tau = 1.0, the performance profile value equals the fraction of solvable scenarios where the algorithm achieves the best (minimum) ERT, possibly tied.
